newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Club agrees Guinea debt restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club agrees Guinea debt restructuring.

text.p: The Paris Club of creditor nations said on Wednesday it agreed to restructure half of Guinea's foreign debt.
It said in a statement it agreed to give Guinea "Naples terms" of debt relief, recommending a treatment providing for debt reduction up to 50 percent.
It said the agreement applied to payments due under loans from, and credits guaranteed by, Guinea's official creditors.
The statement said that representatives of creditor countries noted that Guinea's low per capita income and heavy debt burden called for strong efforts and exceptional treatment of debt.
They also welcomed the implementation in Guinea of an economic reform programme supported by the first annual arrangement under the Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility with the IMF.

"The Paris Club met on February 25 and 26, 1997 with representatives of Guinea. The representatives of the Creditor Countries agreed to recommend to their governments a reorganisation of the maturities falling due during the period covered by Guinea's arrangement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF)," the statement said.
The Paris Club said maturities on Overseas Development Aid loans would be consolidated on a "very long-term basis".
Creditor countries also agreed to meet in three years to consider Guinea's outstanding stock of eligible debt.
The statement said the Paris Club had agreed to give Guinea "Naples terms" of debt relief which are the most generous currently available to poor nations.
But it gave no explanation why Guinea qualified for just 50 percent debt relief rather than 67 percent as would normally be the case under Naples terms.
According to the World Bank Guinea has total debt of $3.19 billion.
